### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.map

### Neovim version

0.12.x

### Description

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8630e862-a225-42ac-bfb8-e2d4c2d17578

When `map.gen_integration.builtin_search()` is enabled, cursor-relative floating windows can sometimes jump to the top-left corner. I noticed this because blink.cmp's completion menu occasionally moves away from the cursor while typing.

It seems that `builtin_search()` temporarily moves the cursor while collecting matches. Although `winrestview()` restores the cursor, the next `nvim_win_set_config({ relative = 'cursor' })` can still use the stale screen position. Running `:redraw` before reconfiguring the float avoids the issue.

Expected behavior: refreshing the search integration should not affect the position of cursor-relative floating windows.

### Reproduction

1. Create a separate `nvim-repro` config directory:

   - `~/.config/nvim-repro/` on Unix
   - `~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/` on Windows

2. Create `init.lua` inside that directory with the following content:

   ```lua
   -- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed)
   vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
   local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath('data')
     .. '/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim'
   local clone_cmd = {
     'git',
     'clone',
     '--depth=1',
     'https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim',
     mini_path,
   }
   vim.fn.system(clone_cmd)
   vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw')

   -- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available
   vim.cmd('packadd mini.nvim')
   require('mini.deps').setup()

   local map = require('mini.map')
   local builtin_search = map.gen_integration.builtin_search()

   map.setup({
     integrations = { builtin_search },
   })

   -- Create enough matching lines to put the cursor in the middle
   -- of the screen while keeping a match on every line.
   local lines = {}
   for i = 1, 120 do
     lines[i] = ('%03d needle'):format(i)
   end

   vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, 0, -1, false, lines)
   vim.bo.modified = false

   -- Activate builtin search highlighting.
   vim.o.hlsearch = true
   vim.fn.setreg('/', 'needle')
   vim.v.hlsearch = 1

   map.open()

   vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { 64, 4 })
   vim.cmd('normal! zz')

   local float_buf = vim.api.nvim_create_buf(false, true)
   vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(
     float_buf,
     0,
     -1,
     false,
     { 'cursor-relative float' }
   )

   local function float_config()
     return {
       relative = 'cursor',
       row = 1,
       col = 0,
       width = 21,
       height = 1,
       style = 'minimal',
       border = 'single',
       focusable = false,
       zindex = 100,
     }
   end

   local float_win

   -- Let MiniMap's initial scheduled refresh finish, flush the
   -- screen state, and then create a correctly positioned float.
   vim.schedule(function()
     vim.cmd('redraw')
     float_win = vim.api.nvim_open_win(
       float_buf,
       false,
       float_config()
     )
   end)

   vim.keymap.set('n', '<Space>', function()
     local before = vim.api.nvim_win_get_position(float_win)

     -- This is the callback produced by
     -- map.gen_integration.builtin_search().
     builtin_search()

     -- Represents another plugin repositioning an already open
     -- cursor-relative window after integration evaluation.
     vim.api.nvim_win_set_config(float_win, float_config())

     local after = vim.api.nvim_win_get_position(float_win)
     local cursor = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)

     vim.notify(vim.inspect({
       before = before,
       after = after,
       cursor = cursor,
     }))
   end)

   -- Control: flushing redraw state before reconfiguring the float
   -- gives it the expected cursor-relative position.
   vim.keymap.set('n', 'gR', function()
     builtin_search()
     vim.cmd('redraw')
     vim.api.nvim_win_set_config(float_win, float_config())

     vim.notify(vim.inspect({
       corrected = vim.api.nvim_win_get_position(float_win),
       cursor = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0),
     }))
   end)
   ```

3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` and wait for the minimap and the `cursor-relative float` window to appear.

4. Confirm that the float is initially displayed directly below the cursor around the middle of the screen.

5. Press `<Space>`.

   The logical cursor remains at `{ 64, 4 }`, but the float moves near the top-left. On an 80x24 headless UI, the measured positions are:

   ```text
   before = { 11, 4 }
   after  = { 1, 0 }
   cursor = { 64, 4 }
   ```

   The exact initial screen row depends on UI height, but `after` resolves against the top screen row instead of the restored cursor row.

6. Press `gR`.

   This evaluates the same integration but executes `:redraw` before `nvim_win_set_config()`. The float is positioned below the cursor again.

- Removing `builtin_search()` from the `<Space>` mapping prevents the issue.
- Running `:nohlsearch` before pressing `<Space>` prevents the issue.
- A redraw must happen before the next cursor-relative window reconfiguration. A redraw alone does not necessarily relocate a float which was already placed incorrectly.

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

> Expected behavior: refreshing the search integration should not affect the position of cursor-relative floating windows.

That's a reasonable expected behavior. Unfortunately the only way (I know of) to get positions of current search matches is by doing iteratively "move cursor to start - search next - search next - ... - search next - restore cursor". There is no way to search relative to some position without changing cursor (as the first paragraph of `:h search()` implies: "The search starts at the cursor position (you can use |cursor()| to set it)"). This is exactly [what 'mini.map' does](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/db41c4076105a63caec12612d11228348f55a109/lua/mini/map.lua#L774-L788).

In theory, this already should not affect floating windows, as cursor is restored right away. But I'll take another look here.

Indeed, there doesn't seem like there is much 'mini.map' can do here for at least two reasons:
- The only way to get the search positions is to iteratively move cursor with `vim.fn.search()`. But 'mini.map' does it responsibly to immediately restore the cursor position and window view as it was before moving cursor.
- Upstream Neovim has (what I believe to be an) issue when it comes to which cursor position it uses when drawing the `relative='cursor'` floating windows: neovim/neovim#40736.

So I think it is safe to close this as both expected behavior and upstream issue.
Ah, thank you for your explanation! Yes, I also think this might be an upstream bug. I'll temporarily disable builtin_search until the upstream is fixed :D

title: [mini.map] `builtin_search` can misplace cursor-relative floating windows
